deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages (handwritten folios 5–6 of this set). We have a family of standard finite ordered sets J_n, indexed by n in N or by a set T of types. We also have a class M of admissible monomorphisms between them, so (J, M) is a small category of 'cell models' C. An 'M-épinglé' ordered set (M-pinned poset) is a poset K with: (i) a type function τ_K : K → N (or T); (ii) for every ξ in K, an isomorphism u^K_ξ : J_{τ_K(ξ)} → K_{≤ξ} onto the lower set of ξ. These identifications must be compatible. For η ≤ ξ, the composite J_{τ(η)} → K_{≤η} ⊂ K_{≤ξ} ≅ J_{τ(ξ)} must be an M-map, and the pinning of K_{≤η} must be the one induced from K_{≤ξ}. The previous page records two facts. A closed (downward-stable) subset of an M-pinned poset carries a unique induced M-pinning making the inclusion admissible. Injective morphisms correspond to monos in the presheaf category Ĉ. Such posets thus model the 'admissible' presheaves on C, i.e. cell complexes whose cells are embedded, in the spirit of regular CW complexes or non-singular semi-simplicial sets.

This page makes two points.
(1) Definition: K is 'of finite type' if Max K is finite and every element of K lies below some maximal element.
(2) Under the second property alone (every element is majorized by a maximal one), an M-pinning is determined by its values u^K_α for α in Max K. This is because each K_{≤ξ} with ξ ≤ α inherits its pinning from that of K_{≤α}, by the closed-subset induction of the previous page.
Conversely, a family of isomorphisms u_α : J_{τ_K(α)} → K_{≤α} (α in Max K) defines a pinning if and only if a gluing condition holds. For all maximal α, β and all ξ ≤ α, β with n = τ_K(ξ), the two isomorphisms J_n → K_{≤ξ} induced from u_α and from u_β must coincide.

This is a descent or gluing statement: a structure on a poset generated by its maximal cells is given by structures on the maximal closed cells that agree on overlaps. It amounts to presenting the admissible object as a colimit, glued along monos, of its maximal cells. The next page then states that admissible objects are stable under arbitrary sums and under amalgamated sums along monos, and that X ↦ X̃ commutes with these operations. It also states that finite-type posets give finite-type objects. The purpose is a combinatorial dictionary between 'admissible' presheaves on a cell category and pinned posets (their posets of non-degenerate cells), presumably as a technical tool in this stack/homotopy-model manuscript.
errors: No real error. The stated condition is necessary, and with the inheritance property from the previous page it is also sufficient: the pinning of each ξ is defined via any maximal α ≥ ξ, and the condition makes this independent of the choice of α. The proof is only implicitly indicated.

The first line as machine-transcribed ('Une catégorie inductive ...') is surely a misreading. From context and the next page's 'objets de type fini', it should define an M-pinned ordered set K 'of finite type'.

ideas.what: Poset of cells with each lower set K_{≤ξ} identified with a standard model J_n via compatible 'épinglages'. This is a combinatorial model of admissible (non-singular) presheaves on a category of cell models.
ideas.modern_name: Face posets of regular CW / non-singular (semi-)simplicial sets; cellular or regular presheaves on a Reedy-type category of monos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face-poset / regular CW correspondence: Björner (1984) and earlier combinatorial topology. Non-singular simplicial sets: Waldhausen–Jahren–Rognes and others.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related themes in Pursuing Stacks (test categories, cellular models), but this exact formalism is not known to me.

ideas.what: Finite type: finitely many maximal elements, each element bounded by a maximal one.
A pinning is determined by its values on maximal cells, subject to agreement on common faces (gluing condition).
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / descent for cell structures; the complex is a colimit of its maximal closed cells

deep.surprise_reason: A routine combinatorial lemma: a pinning of a poset of cells is determined by compatible pinnings of the maximal closed cells. It is a technical step in setting up a poset model for admissible presheaves. Nothing beyond standard gluing arguments; mildly interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's cellular/combinatorial modelling in the 'Champs' notes.
